newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks revert back to losses.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks revert back to losses.

text.p: Argentine stocks switched back to losses Thursday after a three-day recovery from sharp earlier declines, denoting prevailing tension over the direction of U.S. interest rates, dealers said.

"The market rose fast on short-covering but then rubbed up against resistance today and retreated," said Rodrigo Diz at Velox traders. "Cash flows are still not strong enough to push prices higher because institutional investors remain stuck on the sidelines, fearing action from the U.S. Federal Reserve."
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV shed 1.0 percent to 708.70, paring the week's gains to 3.3 percent.
Last week it had dived 5.0 percent to a ten-week low of 686.15.

"The market is caught in a technical band, with a ceiling of 720-730 and a floor of 660," Diz said. "I'd advise people who've made at least a five percent profit to sell and stay liquid until we hit that floor."
Floor volume eased to 19.2 million pesos from 22.1 million Wednesday and 28 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter deals shrank to 102 million against 155.2 million Wednesday.
"This declining trend in volume is a bad thing which leaves the bolsa hostage to Wall Street," another trader said.
The broad market index closed off 0.4 percent, with losers outpacing winners 29 to 20 and 16 issues closing flat.
Sharpest main-tier decliners were carmakers Ciadea and Sevel, which dropped 2.6 percent and 2.1 percent, respectively, and foods giant Molinos and steelmaker Siderar, both off 2.1 percent.
The only MerVal risers were Telecom and Telefonica, which firmed 0.5 percent and 0.3 percent, respectively.
